title: Add a Playwright smoke test
description: Browser smoke test via the Playwright MCP/CI: load the app, assert the WebGL canvas renders, open the panel, switch a preset, and move the points slider. Guards the Three.js/DOM glue that unit tests don't cover.

title: Persist scene to URL and localStorage
description: Serialize transforms + settings (numPoints, colorMode, showGuides) into the URL hash and/or localStorage so a fractal can be shared or restored on reload. Add a pure encode/decode module under src/app with unit tests.

title: Add a color-mode legend overlay
description: Show a small legend/scale for the active color mode (e.g. the height/radius gradient or the per-transform swatches) so the coloring is interpretable. Lives in the app/ui layer.

title: Keyboard shortcuts and accessibility pass
description: Keyboard control for camera/transform editing, focus management for the panel, ARIA on controls, and reduced-motion handling. The panel buttons already carry aria-labels; build on that.

title: Export the fractal as a PNG image
description: Add a button to capture the current view (renderer.domElement.toDataURL) and download it, for sharing renders. Consider a higher-resolution offscreen render.

title: Move the chaos game to a Web Worker
description: Offload runChaosGame + buildColors to a Web Worker (transferable Float32Arrays) so large point counts (up to 500k) don't block the main thread. The pure src/fractal core is already worker-friendly.

title: Add more IFS presets
description: Extend src/fractal/presets.ts with additional named systems (e.g. Barnsley-style fern, Vicsek/cross, dragon curve in 3D) plus buttons in the panel. Pure additions with unit tests for counts/shape.

title: Cinematic Surface lighting: colored area lights and shadowed volumetric shafts
description:
## Image goal

Make existing DE fractals read as places with depth and atmosphere: warm shafts passing through a Menger cathedral, a cool rim separating a dark recursive sculpture from its background, or illuminated mist inside a Balloon cavern. The payoff is a substantially better finished Surface image from an object the app can already render.

## Why this is a new change

Surface already has a directional light, ambient fill, distance fog, a reflected softbox and an emitting checker room. Those do not provide independently positioned colored lights or participating mist whose illumination is occluded by the fractal. The prior finish work found that the lit environment mattered more to the desired image than additional reflection bounces; this proposal builds on that verdict.

## First release

- A small authored Surface light rig, initially a key and a rim light, with position/direction, color, intensity and a finite emitter size where applicable. Light size must affect the surface highlight and shadow softness coherently.
- One bounded homogeneous or height-dependent atmospheric medium with density, tint and scattering directionality. Integrate illumination along the camera ray and query actual DE visibility toward the lights, so geometry opens and closes shafts.
- Progressive settle and still capture using the same light/medium model. The interaction tier may use fewer samples, with its approximation disclosed. Long renders remain cancellable.
- Deliver composed starting scenes with saved cameras, palettes and light rigs, including both native 3D and genuinely non-flat 4D Surface scenes. The feature should make a convincing image immediately, while leaving the rig editable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Before production UI or wire changes, render a matched-camera contact sheet using real DE geometry: existing lighting/fog, new lighting alone, and lighting plus medium. Include a cathedral, a Balloon interior, and a non-flat 4D slice. The owner judges depth, legibility and visual impact; pixel difference alone cannot pass.
2. A light moved behind an occluder changes both surface illumination and its atmospheric shaft. Opening a geometric gap admits light; surface shadow and medium visibility agree.
3. The native 3D scene and the 4D rendered slice use the same displayed-space lighting model. Both Surface engines carry the effect for their supported scene families, with no silent loss on fallback.
4. Zero authored medium density removes only the medium; absent new lighting/medium state preserves the legacy path. Brightness remains stable as sample count, image size and capture-band boundaries change.
5. Saved views, links, scene files, Collection, Timeline and PNG capture reproduce the authored look. Lighting-only changes invalidate every relevant retained frame and accumulation.
6. A production-browser comparison demonstrates the accepted look at ordinary viewport size and high-resolution export. Record convergence, GPU cost, cancellation and memory on verified hardware, including a difficult 4D scene.
design:
Implementation shape: reuse the Surface DE query, shadow contract, linear-light supersampling and capture infrastructure. Add one shared light/medium vocabulary and shader math rather than separate 3D, 4D, GLSL and WGSL definitions. Start by extending scripts/de-preview.ts for the needed reference lighting/scattering hooks; do not create another private sphere marcher.

Scope is direct surface illumination plus single scattering through a bounded medium. It does not depend on the rejected general self-reflection program, nor does it promise glass/refraction or multi-bounce volumetric transport. Existing authored floor/sky radiance remains useful input.

The physical scene for lighting is the displayed three-dimensional space. For 4D content, each visibility query must evaluate the same rotor-posed slice or supported slab that the primary ray draws. Source 4D distance, projected source points and the sliced obstacle are not interchangeable. Retain existing per-family heuristic/certificate status and far-cap rules.

A geometry DE certifies geometry clearance, not zero medium density: an empty-space jump cannot discard fog. Bound the camera/light integration interval, integrate attenuation consistently, and sample scattering/visibility with a declared approximation. Full-image sample coordinates and a deterministic stream must survive tiled PNG rendering without seams.

The new shade state must reach surface-material.ts, surface-material-4d.ts, the shared shade emission in surface-de-gpu.ts, surface-compute.ts and retained-frame/capture invalidation. Identify append-only wire tails at implementation time; preserve existing offsets. Bound nested shadow work in both strip and compute scheduling instead of multiplying the present budget invisibly.

Place authored lights/atmosphere under the Surface Scene / Look controls; sample budget belongs to Renderer and capture to Workflow. Other modes preserve dormant Surface look state with honest applicability. Both dimensional halves and both supported Surface engines are in the same delivery plan and estimate.

Effort/risk: large. Sampling cost and visual convergence are the main risks. This is the recommended first bet for better images from existing fractals. The other two proposals are independent.

Primary references: PBRT's Volume Scattering chapter explains the participating-medium model and Area Lights explains finite-emitter sampling. These support the techniques, not a prediction of this app's speed or artistic result:
https://www.pbr-book.org/4ed/Volume_Scattering
https://pbr-book.org/4ed/Light_Sources/Area_Lights

Project evidence: docs/harness-sheets.md, finish-reflection; src/fractal/surface-finish.ts; src/app/state.ts, SurfaceParams.

title: Sphere-inversion IFS surfaces: recursive pearls, Kleinian lace and vaulted forms
description:
## Image goal

Add a visibly different family of Surface subjects: clusters of recursively nested pearls, perforated spherical shells, and curved vaults with detail repeating through their openings. These should be compelling as simply lit geometry before materials or atmosphere are added.

The construction is an iterated system of sphere inversions. It brings the IFS theme directly into a new visual family; Balloon currently supplies one external inverted echo, while this family makes repeated inversions the structure of the object itself.

## First release

- Prototype a bounded orbit of a seed sphere under a curated collection of disjoint or tangent inversion spheres. A six-sphere 3D arrangement and an eight-hypersphere 4D arrangement are candidate starting fixtures, not accepted parameter domains.
- Define whether a preset depicts the orbit of seed surfaces/solids or an approximation to a group limit set. Keep those objects distinct. Begin with the seed-orbit construction that produces a readable surface.
- Expose a compact family of meaningful controls: generator arrangement, an admitted spacing/radius range, seed size and refinement. Ship several complete Surface presets with saved views and existing materials; camera angle and silhouette are part of the deliverable.
- The native 4D construction uses hypersphere generators acting on xyzw, then the established rotor/slice view. Its slices should reveal new arrangements rather than carry a passive w coordinate through a 3D formula.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The first deliverable is a real DE-rendered beauty/contact sheet in 3D and native 4D, using the shared CPU renderer. The owner must find the geometry both striking and distinct from current Mandelbox, tiling and Balloon results before production integration proceeds.
2. A separate shallow explicit inversion-orbit oracle pins the query algorithm, primitive images and conservative stepping on the admitted domain. An increased-depth reference checks convergence, cusps, near-tangent generators and narrow openings.
3. Inversion centres, non-escaping queries, iteration exhaustion and numerical limits have defined outcomes. No unqualified copied damping factor or local derivative is advertised as a global distance certificate.
4. A genuine non-flat 4D fixture changes under w rotation and offset slicing. A deliberate flat embedding provides the reduction check; literature terminology about four-dimensional groups is not accepted as evidence of this app's xyzw parity.
5. The family is reachable through the real Surface UI and ordinary saved documents. Its params affect geometry, normal, color, shadow and AO consistently; imported unsupported settings are preserved with a clear refusal.
6. CPU and supported shader routes agree, and the authored beauty presets survive fresh load, completed settle and high-resolution PNG capture. Record rendering cost and exhaustion on verified hardware before fixing the public control range.
design:
Research starts with Iterated Inversion Systems rather than assuming that the existing globally contractive affine/fold gate can admit every sphere-inversion group. A whole-space inversion has a pole and is not a contraction. The fundamental domain, generator ordering, seed object, bounded region and stopping rule are part of the geometry definition.

Inspect whether a useful subset can be expressed through the existing per-map affine/fold-radius vocabulary before adding a new core. If it cannot, define a dedicated pure CPU estimator and eligibility resolver with 3D/4D twins, one shared construction vocabulary, and a reachable Surface route. The first delivery slice should settle this representation choice with rendered evidence.

Reuse inversion.ts's inversionBallScale and inversionDistanceLowerBound where their hypotheses hold. Exact transport of a ball away from the pole is stronger evidence than a scalar derivative guessed to work everywhere. Do not apply the helpers to cutoff-shortened distances or bounded regions that cross an inversion centre. A finite orbit approximation and an infinite limit require different remainder arguments.

The Bridges 2016 IIS paper provides a 3D ray-marching construction, but its example includes an empirically selected scale factor. It supplies an algorithmic starting point, not the conservativeness proof or 4D qualification this app needs. Also, four-dimensional Kleinian groups often act on a three-dimensional boundary: independently define and test the proposed R4 scene.

After the visual/domain gate, scope new or extended GLSL/WGSL arms, frozen wire growth, material attribution and bench fixtures together. Mirror shared algebra once. Preserve the existing engine eligibility rules; a newly required route must be disclosed rather than masquerading as an old core. Points/Flame/Solid require a separately justified representation or an explicit Surface-family refusal; a random orbit drawing a different set is not parity.

Use scripts/de-preview.ts for sheets, with actual explicit-orbit or membership instruments where required. Ship 3D and 4D in the same implementation program; a failed 4D feasibility result keeps the capability unfinished rather than converting the plan to 3D-first.

Effort/risk: large to extra large, with the highest mathematical uncertainty of this set. It offers the largest change in the kinds of images the app can make. It does not depend on the new lighting or composition proposals.

Primary references and visual direction:
Nakamura and Ahara, A New Algorithm for Rendering Kissing Schottky Groups, especially the 3D algorithm and its stated damping:
https://archive.bridgesmathart.org/2016/bridges2016-367.pdf
The authors' sphairahedron gallery demonstrates related curved recursive forms; the proposed product family and R4 lift remain to be qualified:
https://sphairahedron.net/

title: Sculpted Surface scenes: compose independent DE fractals and carve architectural forms
description:
## Image goal

Build deliberate compositions with contrasting scales and silhouettes: a smooth stone arch around a dense fractal core, a cut-open recursive tower revealing a second object, or several independently posed fractal forms sharing a floor and casting shadows on each other. Large clean shapes should make the fine IFS detail more dramatic.

## Why this is a new change

Xaos and scheduled hybrids already compose point-generating systems, and ShapeSpec combines primitives for emitters/traps/clipping. Putting multiple forward-orbit maps in today's transform list makes one escape formula chain. This proposal instead keeps each DE object's formula, pose and material independent and combines their rendered fields into one scene.

## First release

- A bounded flat scene composition containing two independently posed DE actors and a small set of analytic bodies/cutters. Each actor owns its own source-system snapshot and exposes translation, rotation, uniform scale and material treatment.
- Start with union and exact analytic sphere/box cut or intersection operations. Support at least an affine IFS actor and a fold-family actor together; shared scene illumination and visibility query the complete composition.
- Provide a few finished compositions with cameras and materials. The authoring model can remain a short part list with transforms; a general node editor is unnecessary to prove the image goal.
- Keep the IFS definitions inside each actor editable. A pose edit moves one whole object without changing its iterative formula or feeding another actor into its orbit.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Before broad UI or shader infrastructure, render an actual DE contact sheet with at least two compelling compositions and native 4D counterparts. Compare against the same actors individually and uncomposed. The owner must judge that composition creates worthwhile new images.
2. Two separately parameterized objects retain their own geometry and material when either is edited. A mixed affine/fold scene must not be evaluated as a single combined escape chain or a point-cloud merge.
3. Visible silhouettes, normals, primary hits, shadow rays and AO all use the same ordered composition. A moved actor occludes the other correctly; cuts produce no floating fragments, accidental caps or stale shadows.
4. The CPU composition agrees with independent primitive/finite-orbit fixtures. Analytic cutter signs are tested on both sides of boundaries; no arbitrary unsigned fractal DE is negated and treated as a signed solid.
5. 4D actors are posed in a common xyzw scene before one global rotor/slice reduction. Off-centre slices and w-mixing rotations exercise both actors and a genuine hypersphere/hyperbox cutter. The flat anchor reproduces the 3D construction.
6. Both applicable Surface engines implement the declared composition domain or explicitly refuse it. Links, files, Collection and Timeline retain every actor; unsupported modes preserve the scene and disclose applicability instead of silently showing only one actor.
7. Real-browser qualification covers completed settle, high-resolution export, cancellation, empty cuts and worst-case overlap. The accepted starter scenes render without special diagnostic flags or hidden source edits.
design:
Use a deliberately capped flat composition, following the existing ShapeSpec packing discipline rather than introducing an unrestricted recursive graph. The spike decides the smallest actor/cutter budget that earns the images; do not freeze a large shader program before measuring its link cost.

A union can query min(dA, dB), retaining hit attribution. Exact signed analytic cutters can restrict a fractal using a max composition, but this does not make the input fractal estimator signed or exact. General fractal-minus-fractal subtraction, smooth Boolean blends and fabricated polished cut caps are outside the first-release domain until their geometry and distance guarantees are defined. Escape-family heuristic inputs remain heuristic after composition; a wrapper does not certify them.

Each actor needs its own bound, pose inverse, estimator params and material namespace. Uniform-scale poses keep distance scaling clear. Bounds can cull irrelevant actors conservatively, while shadow/AO queries still see the full result. Tests must include overlapping actors, ambiguous ties and a cutter that empties an actor. Reuse shared set-membership instruments where available, never volume or DE-threshold guesses about emptiness.

Plan the 3D and 4D CPU composition helpers, surface-material.ts / surface-material-4d.ts integration, WGSL code generation and packing, and Surface routing as one delivery. Mixed cores may create a serious fragment-link cliff; measure both dialects, retain the established 4D compute-only cases, and keep every GPU submission bounded. Per-actor params must not overwrite any frozen existing offsets.

4D posing is part of the authored scene, not a display trick: apply each actor's inverse pose to the common 4D query, then its own estimator. Shared viewing determines the query plane once. Native R4 sphere/box cutters have a direct definition and should precede speculative higher-dimensional torus/mesh operations.

Composition is Scene / Look; render quality is Renderer. Decide the scene-document extension and legacy single-actor identity before implementation. Structural or actor-geometry edits restart affected Surface work; material/pose edits disclose their actual invalidation behavior. Other modes must not substitute an incomplete scene.

Use the existing scripts/de-preview.ts for the first beauty sheet and existing CPU cores as leaves. Start with fixed authored fixtures; expand to the editor only after the visual and cost verdicts. This proposal can ship using today's lighting and materials and has no dependency on the other two ideas.

Effort/risk: extra large. The main cost is multiple-core routing, shared visibility, per-actor storage and shader size in both dimensions. The visual test must justify that cost early.

Project foundations: docs/multi-system-ifs-brief.md (what xaos and schedules mean), src/fractal/shapes.ts (bounded composition and signed primitive semantics), docs/surface-glsl-tracers.md (fragment-link limits), docs/surface-gpu-kernels.md (core/wire contracts).
